'''Alexander B. Gluhovsky''' is an American physicist and statistician known for his contributions to [[geophysical fluid dynamics]], particularly in the development of low-order models for atmospheric and climate phenomena, and for his work in [[computational statistics]] applied to [[time series analysis]] in the [[geoscience]]s. He is a professor emeritus at [[Purdue University]] (in West Lafayette, Indiana) in the Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences, and has a joint appointment in the Department of Statistics as well.<ref name="PurdueEAPS">{{cite web |url=https://www.eaps.purdue.edu/people/profile/aglu.html |title=Alexander Gluhovsky - Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences - Purdue University |publisher=Purdue University |access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref><ref name="PurdueSTAT">{{cite web |url=https://www.stat.purdue.edu/people/faculty/aglu.html |title=Alexander Gluhovsky - Purdue Department of Statistics |publisher=Purdue University |access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Gluhovksy earned his Master of Science (M.S.) in mathematics and statistics from [[Moscow State University]] and received his Ph.D. in applied mathematics from the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]] in 1973.<ref name="PurdueEAPS"/><ref name="PurdueSTAT"/> His doctoral advisor was the prominent Soviet physicist and applied mathematician [[Alexander Obukhov]].<ref name="MGPGluhovsky">{{cite web |title=Alexander B. Gluhovsky |work=Mathematics Genealogy Project |publisher=North Dakota State University |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=30269 |access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>

Gluhovsky's association with Purdue University began in 1992 when he joined the Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences. In 1996 he joined the Department of Statistics as a visiting professor.<ref name="PurdueAppointment">{{cite news |url=https://www.stat.purdue.edu/news/2007/Alexander_Gluhovsky_Associate_Professor_Appointment.html |title=Alexander Gluhovsky Associate Professor Appointment |date=February 1, 2007 |work=Purdue Department of Statistics |publisher=Purdue University |access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref> In 2007, his position was formalized with joint appointments as an associate professor in both departments.<ref name="PurdueAppointment"/> He subsequently achieved the rank of professor and is currently a professor emeritus at the university.<ref name="PurdueEAPS"/>

==Research contributions==
Gluhovsky's research is interdisciplinary, lying at the intersection of [[nonlinear dynamics]], [[atmospheric science]], and [[statistical inference]].

===Low-order models (LOMs)===
A major theme of his work is the formulation and analysis of [[model order reduction|low-order models]] (LOMs) for complex geophysical flows, such as those related to the atmosphere and climate.<ref name="EnergyConserving">{{cite journal |last=Gluhovsky |first=A. |date=2006 |title=Energy-conserving and Hamiltonian low-order models in geophysical fluid dynamics |journal=[[Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics]] |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=125–134 |doi=10.5194/npg-13-125-2006 |bibcode=2006NPGeo..13..125G |doi-access=free |url=https://npg.copernicus.org/articles/13/125/2006/npg-13-125-2006.pdf}}</ref>

He proposed and analyzed LOMs, often in the form of coupled 3-mode nonlinear systems known in mechanics as [[Volterra gyrostats]] (extensions of the [[Lorenz system]]). The equations of the gyrostat, which describe the [[rigid body dynamics|motion of a rigid body]] containing a spinning rotor, are adapted by Gluhovsky as a basis to construct [[geophysical fluid dynamics]] models while ensuring the [[conservation of energy]] and other physical properties.<ref name="EnergyConserving"/> This approach has been applied to model phenomena such as [[Rayleigh-Bénard convection]] (which is related to mesoscale atomospheric dynamics) and the [[El Niño-Southern Oscillation]] (ENSO).<ref name="GyrostaticENSO">{{cite journal |last=Gluhovsky |first=A. |date=2017 |title=A gyrostatic low-order model for the El Ñino–Southern Oscillation |journal=[[Complexity (journal)|Complexity]] |volume=2017 |article-number=6176045 |doi=10.1155/2017/6176045 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

His work connects the dynamic properties of LOMs, such as the existence of [[Lagrangian coherent structure|coherent structures]], to observable features in turbulent flows and atmospheric datasets.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gluhovsky |first1=A. |last2=Tong |first2=C. |last3=Agee |first3=E. |date=2002 |title=Selection of modes in convective low-order models |journal=[[Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences]] |volume=59 |issue=7 |pages=1383–1393 |doi=10.1175/1520-0469(2002)059<1383:SOMICL>2.0.CO;2 |bibcode=2002JAtS...59.1383G }}</ref>

===Subsampling methodology===
Gluhovsky is a notable contributor to the field of computational statistics for time series, particularly through the use of [[resampling (statistics)|resampling]] methods in weather and climate analysis.

He has championed the use of subsampling (a non-parametric resampling technique) to derive reliable confidence intervals and estimates for statistical parameters of highly complex and non-linear atmospheric and climate time series, where traditional parametric methods often fail due to unmet assumptions.<ref name="SubsamplingMethodology">{{cite book |last=Gluhovsky |first=Alexander |date=2008 |chapter=Subsampling Methodology for the Analysis of Nonlinear Atmospheric Time Series |editor=Donner, R. V. |editor2=Barbosa, S. M. |title=Nonlinear Time Series Analysis in the Geosciences |publisher=Springer |volume=112 |pages=3–16 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-78938-3_1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Gluhovsky |first=A. |date=2011 |title=Statistical inference from atmospheric time series: detecting trends and coherent structures |journal=[[Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics]] |volume=18 |issue=4 |pages=537–544 |doi=10.5194/npg-18-537-2011 |bibcode=2011NPGeo..18..537G |doi-access=free }}</ref>

His work has extended these statistical techniques to estimate higher-order moments (such as [[skewness]] and [[kurtosis]]) for nonlinear time series, which are essential for characterizing [[extreme weather]] events.<ref name="Gluhovsky_2009">{{cite journal |last1=Gluhovsky |first1=Alexander |last2=Agee |first2=Ernest |title=Estimating Higher-Order Moments of Nonlinear Time Series |journal=[[Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology]] |volume=48 |issue=9 |pages=1948–1954 |date=September 2009 |doi=10.1175/2009JAMC2124.1 |bibcode=2009JApMC..48.1948G |url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/apme/48/9/2009jamc2124.1.xml |access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>

Gluhovsky has also published research on the effects of land-use/land-cover change on surface temperature trends, employing statistical methods to separate anthropogenic local effects from larger-scale [[climate forcing]].
